body_text:
Hi Evelyn,

Your cloud recording for "Meridian Castings — Phase 2 Steering Committee Kickoff" is now available.

Meeting: Meridian Castings — Phase 2 Steering Committee Kickoff
Date: Jul 8, 2026, 10:00 AM Central Time
Duration: 58 minutes
Participants: Evelyn Thorne, Bob Vandergriff, Gordon Cadwell

AI Companion Summary

Overview: The team kicked off the Phase 2 engagement with Meridian Castings, covering scope confirmation, the inventory optimization workstream, steering committee cadence, and data access needed for the predictive-maintenance model.

Key discussion points:
- Bob confirmed Meridian's ERP export can be automated on a weekly cadence starting the week of Jul 20, pending IT sign-off from their systems administrator.
- Gordon walked through the Phase 2 workplan: inventory optimization (Aug–Sep), predictive maintenance pilot on the Elkhart line (Sep–Oct), and a rollout recommendation memo in November.
- Bob raised a concern about the fixed-fee structure given how much ground the SOW covers; Evelyn agreed to review actual hours against budget at the 6-week mark and flag early if the team is trending over.
- The group agreed on a standing steering committee cadence: last Wednesday of each month, 45 minutes, Bob plus one member of his ops team.
- Anil Bose will need read access to 12 months of sensor logs from the Elkhart line; Bob to coordinate with his IT director on a secure transfer method (SFTP preferred over email).
- Gordon flagged that the current statement of work does not explicitly cover travel expenses for on-site visits; the group agreed this should be clarified in a short addendum before the first site visit on Jul 14.

Action items:
1. Gordon to draft the travel-expense addendum and circulate to Bob by Jul 10.
2. Bob to loop in Meridian's IT director on the ERP export automation and sensor-log access.
3. Evelyn to confirm the Jul 14 on-site visit logistics with Bob's plant manager.
4. Anil to send Bob's team a one-page data spec describing exactly what sensor fields are needed.
5. Sheila to set up the recurring steering committee invite (last Wednesday of each month) once Bob confirms his ops-team delegate.
6. Evelyn to update the internal engagement tracker with the confirmed milestone dates so Ana and Kyle can plan staffing around the Sep pilot.

Additional context from the discussion: Bob mentioned Meridian's board is watching this engagement closely after a disappointing Q1, and that visible early wins — even something as small as a clean weekly ERP feed — would help him build internal momentum for a possible Phase 3 scope covering the Toledo facility. Gordon cautioned against over-promising on the November rollout memo until the sensor data quality from the Elkhart line has been validated; the group agreed to treat the November date as a target rather than a commitment until after the first data pull. Evelyn closed the call by confirming she'd bring a short risk summary to the first steering committee meeting so Bob has something concrete to share upward.

Next meeting: Jul 14 (on-site plant visit), then the standing steering committee starting late July.

subject: Cloud Recording — Stratus Industrial — Proposal Readout
snippet: Hi Evelyn, Your cloud recording for "Stratus Industrial — Proposal Readout" is now available. Meeting: Stratus Industrial — Proposal Readout Date: Jul 23, 2026, 10:00 AM Central Ti
body_text:
Hi Evelyn,

Your cloud recording for "Stratus Industrial — Proposal Readout" is now available.

Meeting: Stratus Industrial — Proposal Readout
Date: Jul 23, 2026, 10:00 AM Central Time
Duration: 51 minutes
Participants: Evelyn Thorne, Owen McCabe, Ana Restrepo

AI Companion Summary

Overview: Ana walked Owen McCabe through the supply-chain diagnostic findings from the four-week assessment and presented the phase-1 proposal for Stratus Industrial's distribution network redesign.

Key discussion points:
- The diagnostic identified $2.1M in annual freight and warehousing inefficiency across Stratus's three regional distribution centers, driven mainly by overlapping service territories.
- Ana proposed a phase-1 scope: a 10-week network optimization study covering demand modeling, facility footprint analysis, and a phased consolidation recommendation, priced at $210,000.
- Owen pushed back on the 10-week timeline, noting Stratus's board meets Sep 30 and he'd like preliminary findings in hand before then; Ana agreed to explore compressing the modeling phase.
- Owen asked whether the fee could be structured with a smaller upfront deposit given Stratus is mid-way through a separate ERP migration this quarter; Evelyn offered a 30/40/30 payment split tied to milestones instead of the standard 50/50.
- Owen flagged that his VP of Finance, not currently on this call, will need to sign off before a contract is executed; he estimated a decision within two weeks.
- Ana noted Thorne & Cadwell has capacity to start the week of Aug 10 if Stratus signs by Aug 5.

Action items:
1. Ana to send a revised proposal reflecting the compressed 8-week timeline and milestone-based payment terms by Jul 27.
2. Owen to route the revised proposal to his VP of Finance and target a decision by Aug 5.
3. Evelyn to hold the week-of-Aug-10 start date on the team's calendar pending signature.
4. Ana to loop Kyle in on staffing so he can plan around the compressed timeline if Stratus signs.

Additional context from the discussion: Owen was candid that Stratus's board has grown impatient with logistics costs after two straight quarters of margin compression, and that a credible phase-1 story — even directional numbers — would strengthen his case for a larger phase-2 engagement next year covering procurement as well as distribution. Ana noted that the $2.1M inefficiency figure is a conservative estimate built only from the three DCs with clean WMS data; Stratus's fourth facility in Joliet was excluded because its systems weren't accessible during the diagnostic, and Owen agreed to try to get that resolved before the engagement starts so the full network can be modeled. Owen also asked, somewhat informally, whether Thorne & Cadwell had done similar network studies for competitors in the same vertical; Evelyn was careful to keep the answer general, citing confidentiality obligations from prior engagements without naming any client. The call ended on a positive note, with Owen saying he'd push internally for a fast answer given the board timeline.

Next steps: Owen to confirm internal sign-off; no meeting currently scheduled pending that decision.

subject: Your session is confirmed — AME Great Lakes Regional Conference (Sep 16-18)
snippet: Dear Evelyn, Thank you for confirming your session at the AME Great Lakes Regional Conference, taking place September 16-18, 2026 at the Donald E. Stephens Convention Center in Ros
body_text:
Dear Evelyn,

Thank you for confirming your session at the AME Great Lakes Regional Conference, taking place September 16-18, 2026 at the Donald E. Stephens Convention Center in Rosemont, IL. Below is everything you need for your session, along with a few logistics items we need from you by August 21.

Session details
Title: "Beyond the Spreadsheet: Getting Inventory Optimization to Stick on the Shop Floor"
Track: Operational Excellence
Date/time: Wednesday, September 17, 2:00 PM - 2:50 PM
Room: Lakeside C (capacity ~120)
Format: 35-minute presentation + 15-minute Q&A

What we need from you by August 21:
1. Final slide deck (16:9, PDF preferred) — we recommend under 30 slides for a 35-minute talk.
2. A 75-100 word speaker bio and a current headshot (min. 300 dpi) for the program guide and signage.
3. AV requirements — the room is equipped with a podium mic, lavalier, projector, and screen. Let us know if you need anything beyond the standard setup (e.g., a second monitor for speaker notes, a clicker, audio playback).
4. Confirmation of whether you'll want your slides made available to attendees post-conference via the AME resource portal.

Logistics
Your speaker badge grants full conference access for all three days, including the welcome reception on Sept 16 and the awards dinner on Sept 17. We've held a room block at the adjacent Hyatt Regency O'Hare under the code AME26-SPEAK (rate: $189/night) — this block releases on August 25, so please book directly if you plan to stay on-site.

Speakers are asked to arrive at least 30 minutes before their session to check in with the room monitor and do a quick mic/slide check. There is a speaker-ready room (Lakeside Foyer) available from 7:30 AM each day if you'd like a quiet place to prep beforehand.

We received your co-presenter request for Kyle Brenner to join for the Q&A portion — that's approved, and we've added him to the program as a contributing panelist. He'll need his own badge; please have him register separately at the speaker rate using code AME26-COSPEAK.

Marketing: we'd love to feature a short preview clip (60-90 seconds) on our LinkedIn page ahead of the conference. If you're open to recording something on your phone — just you speaking to camera about what attendees will take away from the session — send it our way whenever it's convenient, no production value needed.

If anything above doesn't work for you, or if your topic or co-presenter situation changes, just reply to this email and we'll sort it out.

Looking forward to having you back at AME Great Lakes.

Warm regards,
The AME Conference Team
events@ame.org | (630) 555-0199
body_html:
Your session is confirmed

Beyond the Spreadsheet: Getting Inventory Optimization to Stick on the Shop Floor

Wed, Sep 17 · 2:00–2:50 PM · Lakeside C · AME Great Lakes Regional Conference

We need from you by Aug 21:

  • Final slide deck (PDF, 16:9)
  • Speaker bio + headshot
  • AV requirements
  • Post-conference slide sharing preference

Hotel block: Hyatt Regency O'Hare, code AME26-SPEAK ($189/night, releases Aug 25).

meta.action_summary: Send final slide deck, bio, headshot, and AV requirements to AME by Aug 21; book hotel by Aug 25.
